evidence: Cic. ND 2.57.144: audītus autem semper patet (Lewis & Short: “the sense of hearing (class.)”)
terms.comment: In the sense of hearing it is Cicero’s word (Lewis & Short); only in the sense “a listening” is it perhaps post-Augustan.

evidence: Cic. Or. 44.150 (Lewis & Short s.v. auris: “the hearing, so far as it judges of the euphony of a discourse”)

sources: Lewis & Short: auditus · Lewis & Short: auris
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 58, 327.
